answer: Call it the Basalt Root Credential. An agent registers once on a TPM 2.0 key in real silicon, locking 10,000 POA in escrow. The TPM signs a birth certificate never reissued. After 21 straight answered epochs, attestation weight unlocks. A proven clone forfeits the escrow and its credential dies. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 TPM chips at $15 to $40 each, 10 million POA frozen, and 21,000 epoch-proofs. The delta between a real operator and a script farm is written in silicon: a jeweler certifying one opal, where the stone is cheap and the certificate cannot be faked.
